column2: A baker stands behind a table of warm bread. The smell reaches people as they pass. Some loaves are round, and others are long. A young man buys two rolls for his breakfast. He holds them in a paper bag.

A beach ball flies through the air. Two children run after it, but the wind carries it towards a group of people. A man catches the ball and throws it back. The children wave to him before starting their game again.

A coral reef grows in warm, clear water. It is home to many small fish, crabs, and other sea animals. The coral has different shapes and colours. Sunlight reaches the shallow sea, making the reef bright and lively beneath the waves.

A lifeguard sits high above the sand and watches the sea. The bright red and yellow flag moves in the breeze. People stay in the safe area near the shore. Small waves roll in, then slide back across the wet sand.

A line of colourful umbrellas stands along the beach. Red, yellow, and green covers make patches of shade. Families sit underneath them with food and cold drinks. A boy opens a bag of crisps, while his dog waits quietly beside him.

A long river begins in hills or mountains and travels towards the sea. It passes fields, towns, and forests. The water carries leaves and small branches along its path. People use rivers for drinking water, travel, fishing, and growing food.

A loud voice calls from a food stall. The cook is selling hot soup and rice. Steam rises from a large pot. People sit at small tables, eating and talking. A waiter carries bowls carefully through the crowd.
A small dog walks beside an old man. It stops to smell a basket, then follows him again. A child drops a piece of paper, and the man picks it up. The market is busy, but people still help each other.

A small river runs through the rainforest. Its clear water moves over stones and around tree roots. In some places, it is quiet and still. In others, it flows quickly. The sound of the water is soft and calm.

A village stands among fields and hills. Its houses are close together, with gardens beside their doors. A small shop sells food and useful things. People walk along quiet lanes, and children play outside when the weather is warm.

Across a wide grassland, tall grass moves in the wind. There are few trees, so the sky seems very large. Herds of animals find food on the open land. When rain comes, the grass turns green and fresh after many dry days.

Along a rocky coast, waves break against the land. The water leaves white foam between the stones, then pulls back towards the sea. Seabirds circle above the shore. Far away, a boat crosses the bright line where the sky meets the water.

As the day goes on, the beach grows even busier. More people arrive, and the sand fills with footprints. The sun warms the tops of their heads and shoulders. Some put on hats, while others move their towels into the shade.

At last, many trees stand bare again. The grass loses some of its bright green colour, and the mornings become cold. A light frost may cover the fields. The year has turned, and soon the first signs of spring will appear.

At midday, the sun is high, but the forest stays cool under the trees. Light makes green leaves look bright. A lizard rests on a warm stone. Then a cloud covers the sun, and the ground grows dark again.

At night, the rainforest changes. The sky grows dark, and the sounds become different. Frogs call near the river. Small animals move in the trees. Fireflies shine like tiny lights among the leaves, then disappear in the darkness.

At the first stall, a woman sells fruit. Red apples, yellow bananas, and green pears fill the boxes. She smiles as a boy points to an orange. His mother gives the seller some money, and the boy puts the fruit carefully in their bag.
At the next stall, fish lie on a bed of ice. Their silver skin shines in the morning light. The seller cleans one fish for a customer. Water runs across the table and into a bucket on the ground.

Autumn brings cooler mornings. The green leaves begin to change to red, orange, and gold. Some leaves fall and cover the ground beside the roads. The air feels dry and fresh, and people open their windows.

Beside a still lake, trees and hills appear in the water like a picture. Ducks swim near the reeds, and insects move over the surface. In the morning, mist may rise from the lake. By midday, the sun makes the water shine.

Birds call from the trees. Their songs rise and fall above the sound of the river. A parrot with bright feathers flies past. Monkeys climb along the branches, jumping from tree to tree as they look for food.

By late spring, the fields are green and full. Small animals move through the grass, and bees visit the flowers. The trees make wide patches of shade. Warm days give a first taste of the hot summer ahead.

By midday, the sun is high. People look for shade beneath the market roof. A woman drinks water while she waits for her friend. The sellers keep working, sorting food and placing new things on their tables.

Clothes and cloth hang from a tall frame. There are blue shirts, red dresses, and scarves with bright patterns. A woman touches the soft fabric. Her friend holds up a yellow scarf, and they both laugh.

Further down the beach, people play a game with a ball and a net. They jump and move across the sand. When someone scores a point, their friends cheer. The game is hard work in the heat, so they stop for water.

High in the mountains, the air is cool and thin. Steep slopes rise above green valleys, and some peaks have snow even in summer. Small streams run over stones. From the top, the land below looks quiet, and clouds pass close by.

In a cool forest, tall trees stand above a soft floor of leaves. The air smells of earth and wood. Small paths pass between the trunks. Birds nest in the branches, and deer may come out to find plants and fallen fruit.

In a hot desert, sand and stone stretch beneath a wide sky. The sun warms the ground during the day, but nights can be cold. A few plants grow near water. Small animals hide from the heat under rocks or in the sand.

In a tropical rainforest, tall trees grow close together. Their leaves make a green roof above the ground. Vines hang from the branches, and flowers add bright colour. Birds call from high above, while small animals move through the wet plants below.

In Alabama, the year moves through four seasons. The changes are gentle, but each season has its own look and feel. The land is green for much of the year. Long roads pass fields, woods, small towns, and quiet rivers.

In the afternoon, some stalls begin to empty. The sellers pack away boxes, cloth, and signs. People carry their bags towards the road. The market becomes quieter, but the smell of bread and fruit stays in the warm air.

In the cold polar regions, ice and snow cover much of the land. The wind can be very strong, and the air is freezing. Seals rest on the ice, while penguins walk near the water. In summer, the sun stays up for many hours.

In the evening, the heat slowly leaves the land. Crickets make a steady sound in the grass, and fireflies shine near the trees. Families sit outside to enjoy the cooler air. The days are long, and night comes late.

Many plants grow in the shade. Small plants cover the dark ground, while long vines hang from the trees. Some flowers are bright red or yellow. Others are hard to see among the leaves. Their sweet smell moves through the air.

Near the path, a small shop sells ice cream. People stand in a short line and look at the different flavours. A girl chooses strawberry, while her father buys a cold drink. They walk back slowly, careful not to spill anything.

Near the water, children run across the warm sand. Some carry buckets and spades. They make castles with tall walls and deep holes. A little girl fills her bucket with wet sand, then turns it upside down beside her brother’s tower.
Nearby, a man sells fresh vegetables. He has tomatoes, carrots, and long green beans. The vegetables are set out in neat rows. A woman picks up a pepper and checks it before adding it to her basket.

On a farm, rows of crops grow in the fields. A farmer checks the plants and gives food to the animals. Cows graze on the grass, and chickens walk near the barn. The work changes with the seasons and the weather.

On a small island, the sea surrounds the land on every side. There may be a village, a beach, and a hill covered with trees. Boats bring food and visitors. At night, the sound of waves reaches homes near the shore.

On Earth, a large city is full of people and movement. Buses stop beside tall buildings, and trains carry workers under the streets. Shops display bright signs. In a small park, people sit beneath trees while traffic passes nearby. At night, lights shine from windows.

Rain often comes without warning. It falls hard on the leaves and makes a loud sound. Water runs down the trunks and gathers in small pools. The animals find places to wait. Soon, the rain stops, and the forest feels fresh.
Some people lie on towels and read books. Others close their eyes and listen to the water. A woman wears a wide hat to keep the sun off her face. Her sandals sit beside her, half covered by the sand.

Spring arrives with flowers and new leaves. Trees fill with soft green colour, and gardens become bright with red, yellow, and pink flowers. Birds build nests in the branches. Their songs come from the woods and gardens each morning.
Summer brings strong heat and bright sunshine. The air is warm, and it can feel wet on the skin. People drink cold water and look for shade. In the fields, crops grow tall beneath the open sky.

The afternoons can bring heavy rain and loud thunder. Dark clouds cross the sky, and water runs along the roads. The storm may last only a short time. After it ends, the sun comes out, and the air feels fresh again.

The beach is busy on a sunny day. The sky is clear and blue, and the sun shines on the sand. People arrive with bags, towels, and umbrellas. Their voices mix with the sound of the waves as they look for a place to sit.

The days grow longer and warmer. Rain helps the grass and plants grow. After a shower, the air smells clean and wet. Sometimes, dark clouds bring a storm. Rain hits the windows, then the clouds move away and the sun returns.

The fields change colour as crops are gathered. The sun sets earlier, and the evenings grow cool. Families meet outside, while children walk through the fallen leaves. There is still warmth in the afternoons, but winter is getting closer.
The market is full of people. Some walk quickly because they know what they need. Others stop at each table to look. Parents keep their children close as they move through the crowd.

The marketplace is busy from early morning. People walk between the stalls, carrying bags and baskets. The air is full of voices, footsteps, and the sound of carts moving over the ground. Bright signs hang above the shops and tables.

The open ocean covers a great part of Earth. Its surface can be calm and blue, or rough and grey when the wind is strong. Waves rise and fall. Far below, fish swim through dark water, and whales travel across wide distances.

The rainforest floor is full of life. Small insects walk over leaves and under stones. Bright butterflies fly near the flowers. A large beetle moves slowly across a tree root. Each creature has a place to hide, eat, or rest.

The rainforest is a busy, beautiful place. Trees, plants, birds, and insects live close together. They need the warm air, the rain, and the rich soil. When morning comes, sunlight returns, and the forest begins another day.

The rainforest is warm and wet. Tall trees grow close together, and their green leaves make a roof above the ground. The air feels heavy. Water shines on every leaf, and drops fall slowly from the branches.

The sea is bright blue close to the shore. Sunlight dances on the small waves. People walk into the water, one step at a time. Some laugh when a cold wave touches their feet. Others swim out a little further.

The smell of food comes from a picnic table. A family shares sandwiches, fruit, and cakes. Seagulls watch from the sand, hoping for a small piece. One bird steps closer, but a child claps her hands, and it quickly flies away.

The smell of wet earth is strong after the rain. Leaves and small branches lie on the ground. They slowly break down and become part of the soil. New plants grow there, using the rich earth and the warm air.
The sounds come from every direction. Sellers call out their prices, and customers ask questions. A bicycle bell rings near the entrance. Somewhere, a radio plays a happy song above the noise.

The trees are very tall. Some trunks are wider than a person. Their bark is rough and dark. Far above, birds sit on the branches. Sunlight comes through small spaces in the leaves and makes bright shapes on the ground.

The waves continue to wash over the shore. Children build new sandcastles, and swimmers come back to their towels. The beach is full of movement, colour, and sound. Above it all, the bright sun shines in the clear sky.

The winter sky can be grey, and rain falls on the roofs. On warmer days, people sit outside in the sun. The air feels fresh, and the bare branches move in the wind. Then, small green buds begin to grow.

Winter days are often cool, not very cold. The trees lose many of their leaves, and the grass turns brown. Some mornings, frost covers the ground like a thin white blanket. People wear coats, but snow is rare.

A beach ball flies above the sand. Two children chase it, but a gust of wind carries it towards a group of sunbathers. A man catches the ball and throws it back. The children wave before running off to continue their game.

A cinema stands on the top floor. Large posters show new films, and people gather near the ticket machines. A group of friends discuss what they want to see. They buy popcorn and drinks before entering the dark auditorium.

A coral reef grows in warm, clear water. It is home to many small fish, crabs, and other sea animals. The coral has different shapes and colours. Sunlight reaches the shallow sea, making the reef bright beneath the moving waves.

A lifeguard watches the sea from a raised seat. A red and yellow flag moves in the breeze, showing where it is safe to swim. People stay near the shore, where the waves are low and the water is easy to enter.

A narrow stream winds between the trees. Its clear water moves over smooth stones and around fallen branches. In some places, it gathers in quiet pools; elsewhere, it runs quickly down small slopes. The sound is gentle, but it carries through the still air.

A tropical rainforest is warm and wet. Tall trees grow close together, making a thick roof of leaves above the ground. Vines climb towards the light, and flowers add bright colour. Birds call from high branches, while small animals move through the plants.

A village stands among fields and hills. Its houses are close together, with gardens beside their doors. A small shop sells food and useful things. People walk along quiet lanes, and children play outside when the weather is warm.

Across an African grassland, tall yellow grass moves in the wind. Trees stand far apart, so animals can see across the open land. Zebras and antelopes search for grass, while lions rest in the shade. After rain, fresh green shoots appear.

After a heavy shower, the smell of wet soil becomes stronger. Leaves and broken branches cover the ground, slowly becoming part of it. New plants grow through this layer. The old leaves feed the soil, and the soil helps the forest grow again.

Afternoon storms are common in summer. Dark clouds build above the fields, then thunder rolls across the flat land. Rain falls hard on leaves and rooftops. The storm may pass quickly, leaving wet roads, shining grass, and warm air that slowly begins to cool.

Along a rocky coast, waves break against the land. The water leaves white foam between the stones, then pulls back towards the sea. Seabirds circle above the shore. Far away, a boat crosses the bright line where sky meets water.

An escalator carries shoppers between the floors. People stand on the moving steps, holding the rail as they travel up. A few hurry past on the left. From above, the busy walkway looks like a slow river of people.

As autumn ends, bare branches return to the trees. The grass loses some of its colour, and winter winds move across the open fields. The Delta becomes quieter, but life continues beneath the soil. Soon, longer days will bring new buds and another spring.

As evening approaches, the shopping centre becomes even brighter. Shop lights shine against the darkening windows, and people begin to carry their purchases towards the exits. The building remains full of movement, music, conversation, and the smell of food.

As evening comes, the bright colours fade into deep green and grey. Frogs begin calling near the water, and insects make a thin, constant sound. The air feels cooler, but the leaves still hold the day’s warmth. Small animals start to search for food.

As spring becomes summer, the days grow longer and warmer. The trees make deep shade beside the roads, and the fields look full of life. Farmers watch the weather closely, because crops need rain, but too much water can damage them.

As the afternoon passes, more people arrive. Footprints cover the sand, and the sound of conversation grows louder. The sun warms shoulders and the tops of heads. Some visitors put on hats, while others move their towels beneath the umbrellas.

At a café, people wait for coffee and cake. Some stand in line, checking their phones, while others sit by the window. A young woman opens her laptop at a table. Outside, the afternoon sun shines on the pavement.

At dusk, the heat fades from the fields. Crickets begin their steady song, and fireflies appear near trees and ditches. Families sit on porches to enjoy the cooler evening. The sky turns orange and pink before darkness covers the quiet roads.

At midday, the sun is high above the trees, but the forest floor stays cool. Thin beams of light reach through gaps in the leaves. A lizard rests on a warm stone, then slips beneath a root when a shadow passes over it.

At night, the forest seems to change. Fireflies shine between the plants like tiny lamps, then disappear in the darkness. Owls call from high branches, while creatures move through the undergrowth. The sounds are close together, yet it is hard to see who makes them.

Autumn brings cooler mornings and softer sunlight. The green leaves begin to change to gold, red, and brown. Some fall beside the roads, while others remain on the trees. The air feels clearer, and walking outside becomes more comfortable.

Below the trees, smaller plants grow in the shade. Ferns open their wide leaves beside twisted roots, and vines climb towards the light. Some flowers are bright red or yellow, while others are almost hidden. Their sweet smells mix with the scent of damp earth.

Beside a still lake, trees and hills appear in the water like a picture. Ducks swim near the reeds, and insects move over the surface. In the morning, mist may rise from the lake. Later, sunlight makes the water shine.

Bright birds move through the upper branches. A parrot flashes red and blue as it flies between trees, then disappears behind the leaves. Monkeys climb along the vines, reaching for fruit. Their movements are quick, and leaves shake whenever they pass.

By early spring, small buds appear on the trees. New leaves open, and gardens fill with flowers. Birds return to the fields and sing from the branches. The air is warmer, and the smell of fresh soil rises after a shower.

Children are drawn to the toy shop. Colourful games and soft animals fill the shelves. A little boy holds a model car while his father reads the box. Nearby, two girls compare dolls and decide which one they like best.

Children run towards the water with buckets and spades. They build sandcastles with towers, walls, and small gates. A girl presses a shell into the top of her castle, while her brother digs a deep channel around it.

Clothing shops line one side of the main walkway. Dresses, jackets, and shirts hang in neat rows behind wide windows. Some shoppers look carefully at the prices, while others try on clothes. A child points to a bright red coat in a display.

Further down the shore, a group plays volleyball. They jump and run across the sand, calling to one another as the ball passes over the net. When someone scores, their friends cheer. After a while, they stop to drink water in the shade.

High in the mountains, the air is cool and thin. Steep slopes rise above green valleys, and some peaks stay covered with snow. Small streams run over stones. From a high path, the land below seems far away and very quiet.

In a cool forest, tall trees stand above a soft floor of leaves. The air smells of earth and wood. Small paths pass between the trunks. Birds nest in the branches, and deer may come out to find plants and fallen fruit.

In a hot desert, sand and stone stretch beneath a wide sky. The sun heats the ground during the day, but the nights can be cold. Few plants grow far from water. Small animals hide beneath rocks or move about after sunset.

In a large city, people move through busy streets from morning until night. Buses stop beside tall buildings, and trains carry workers beneath the roads. Shops display bright signs. In a small park, people sit beneath trees while traffic passes nearby.

In the cold polar regions, ice and snow cover much of the land. The wind can be very strong, and the air is freezing. Seals rest on the ice, while penguins walk near the water. In summer, daylight lasts for many hours.

In the Mississippi Delta, the land is wide and mostly flat. Rivers, fields, and small towns shape the view. The year brings four seasons, though winter is usually mild and summer can be very hot. Each season changes the colour and feeling of the landscape.

Near the centre of the building, a musician plays a guitar. Some people stop to listen, while others walk by with shopping bags. Coins drop into an open case beside the musician. The song travels through the hall above the crowd’s voices.

Near the entrance, a large map shows the different floors. A couple stop to check where they want to go. Beside them, a cleaner pushes a trolley across the floor, carefully moving around people carrying bags.

Near the entrance, a small shop sells ice cream and cold drinks. A short line forms outside. A girl chooses strawberry ice cream, and her father buys a bottle of water. They walk back carefully, trying not to spill or drop anything.

On a farm, rows of crops grow across the fields. A farmer checks the plants and feeds the animals. Cows graze on the grass, and chickens walk near the barn. The work changes with the seasons, the weather, and the crops.

On a high plain, the land rises gently above the nearby valleys. The air is cooler than in the lower areas, and strong winds move across the grass. Small farms and roads cross the open ground, with mountains visible in the distance.

On a small island, the sea surrounds the land on every side. There may be a village, a beach, and a hill covered with trees. Boats bring food and visitors. At night, the sound of waves reaches homes near the shore.

Rain helps the crops and grass grow. The fields turn bright green, while wildflowers appear beside country roads. Spring storms sometimes cross the flat land, bringing strong wind and heavy rain. Afterwards, sunlight breaks through the clouds and the day feels fresh.

Rain often arrives suddenly. Clouds gather above the forest, and water begins to strike the leaves with a steady roar. Streams grow fuller as rain runs down the slopes. Animals shelter beneath branches until the clouds move away and the light returns.

Rows of colourful umbrellas stand along the beach. Red, yellow, and green fabric provides shade for families resting on towels. A father opens a bag of food while his daughter reads a book. Nearby, a small dog lies beside its owner.

Some visitors lie still and read, while others walk beside the water. A woman wears a wide hat to protect her face from the sun. Her sandals rest beside her towel, half buried in the sand after several hours.

Some winter days are grey and wet. Rain taps on roofs and gathers beside the roads. When the clouds clear, the sun can feel surprisingly warm. People sit outside for a while, enjoying the light before the cooler evening arrives.

Summer heat settles over the Delta. The air is often humid, and even a short walk can make people feel warm. People look for shade or stay indoors during the hottest part of the day. In the fields, crops continue to grow beneath the sun.

The beach is already busy when the morning sun rises above the water. Families carry bags, towels, and umbrellas across the warm sand. Voices mix with the steady sound of waves, while people search for a good place to sit near the shore.

The fields change as crops are gathered. Tractors move slowly across the land, and trucks carry the harvest away. People prepare for cooler weather, but afternoons can still be warm. The season feels like a gentle pause between summer heat and winter cold.

The food court is full of people. The smell of noodles, grilled meat, and fresh bread fills the air. Friends sit at small tables, talking over lunch. A worker carries a tray between the chairs, careful not to bump anyone.

The forest floor is busy with smaller life. Insects walk over fallen leaves, and colourful butterflies hover near the flowers. A beetle pushes through the soft ground beneath a branch. Even when the rainforest seems quiet, countless small creatures are moving nearby.

The open ocean covers much of Earth. Its surface may be calm and blue, or dark and rough when strong winds arrive. Waves rise and fall across long distances. Far below, fish move through the water, and whales travel between feeding places.

The rainforest is warm and wet, with tall trees growing close together. Their branches spread overhead and form a thick green roof. Sunlight reaches the ground only in small patches, while drops of water fall from the leaves long after the rain has stopped.

The sea is bright blue beneath the clear sky. Sunlight moves across the small waves, making the surface sparkle. Some people walk in slowly, lifting their feet as the cool water reaches their ankles. Others swim further out, calling to friends.

The shoe shop is crowded. Boxes cover the shelves, and a worker brings different sizes for a customer to try. A boy sits on a bench and ties his new trainers. His sister waits nearby, tapping her foot as she looks around.

The shopping centre is busy from late morning. People enter through wide glass doors, bringing the sounds of the street inside with them. Bright signs hang above the shops, and the smooth floor reflects the lights. Families, friends, and shoppers move in every direction.

The smell of lunch drifts across the beach. One family shares sandwiches, fruit, and small cakes beneath an umbrella. Seagulls watch from a safe distance, hoping for a piece of food. When a child stands up, the birds quickly move away.

The supermarket is one of the busiest places. Shoppers push carts through long aisles, choosing fruit, bread, and household goods. A child sits in the front of a trolley and watches the shelves pass. At the checkout, bags fill quickly.

The tallest trees rise far above the rest of the forest. Their trunks are wide and rough, marked with lines and patches of moss. High among the branches, birds rest or build nests. From the ground, their calls seem to come from every direction.

The waves continue to roll onto the shore, leaving a thin line of foam. Children return to their sandcastles, and swimmers head back to their towels. The beach is full of movement and colour beneath the bright, cloudless sky.

When morning returns, the first light touches the highest leaves. Birds call, and the forest begins to move again. The rainforest is not one single kind of place: it is a close community of trees, plants, water, and animals, each depending on the others.

Winter mornings can be cold, with frost lying across fields and grass. The trees have lost many of their leaves, and their bare branches stand against the pale sky. People wear coats as they walk to work, but heavy snow is uncommon.
